apis.name: VirtualAlloc
apis.summary: Reserves, commits, or changes the state of a region of pages in the calling process's virtual address space.
apis.description: VirtualAlloc manages virtual memory in the calling process. Reserving sets aside a range of the address space without charging physical storage; committing makes pages accessible and backed by physical storage or the paging file. The system rounds addresses and sizes to page boundaries, and newly committed pages are zero-initialized. A single call can reserve and commit a region, which is the common case.
apis.prototype: LPVOID VirtualAlloc(LPVOID lpAddress, SIZE_T dwSize, DWORD flAllocationType, DWORD flProtect);

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The requested starting address for the region, or NULL to let the system choose one. With MEM_RESERVE the address is rounded down to the nearest allocation granularity; with MEM_COMMIT it is rounded down to the nearest page boundary.

parameters.name: dwSize
parameters.description: The size of the region, in bytes. When lpAddress is NULL, the system rounds the size up to the next page boundary; otherwise every page containing part of the range is included, so a range that straddles a page boundary affects both pages.

parameters.name: flAllocationType
parameters.description: The allocation operation, such as MEM_RESERVE, MEM_COMMIT, or both. Other documented flags control large pages, write tracking, and reset behavior. MEM_COMMIT without MEM_RESERVE commits pages inside an existing reserved region.

parameters.name: flProtect
parameters.description: The memory protection for the committed pages, such as PAGE_READWRITE or PAGE_EXECUTE_READ. Protection applies when pages are committed; reserved pages are not accessible regardless of this value.

return.success: The base address of the allocated region.
return.failure: NULL. Call GetLastError for the error code.

apis.remarks: Addresses returned by VirtualAlloc are page-aligned and valid only in the calling process. Reserving a region does not make it accessible; access requires a successful commit. Pages that are decommitted and later recommitted are zeroed again, so their previous contents should not be relied on.
apis.maldev_notes: VirtualAlloc is a standard memory-management API that also appears frequently in analysis of code that creates private memory regions. Analysts often record the allocation type, protection, size, and whether the region is later written to or executed. The call alone is not evidence of malicious behavior.
apis.defensive_notes: Allocation telemetry and memory maps can show private regions and their protection. Context such as the allocating module, call stack, protection changes, and later execution is more meaningful than the allocation itself.

apis.name: VirtualFree
apis.summary: Releases or decommits a region of pages in the calling process's virtual address space.
apis.description: VirtualFree changes the state of pages previously allocated with VirtualAlloc. Decommitting releases the physical storage behind committed pages while leaving the address range reserved, so the pages can be committed again later. Releasing frees the entire reserved region, after which the address range is no longer part of the process's allocations.
apis.prototype: BOOL VirtualFree(LPVOID lpAddress, SIZE_T dwSize, DWORD dwFreeType);

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The base address of the region to free. When dwFreeType is MEM_RELEASE, this must be the base address returned by VirtualAlloc.

parameters.name: dwSize
parameters.description: The size of the region to free, in bytes. It must be zero when dwFreeType is MEM_RELEASE. With MEM_DECOMMIT, every page containing part of the range is decommitted, and a size of zero with the region's base address decommits the entire allocation.

parameters.name: dwFreeType
parameters.description: The free operation: MEM_DECOMMIT releases physical storage but keeps the range reserved, while MEM_RELEASE frees the entire reserved region. The two flags cannot be combined.

return.success: A nonzero value; the pages were decommitted or the region was released.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: MEM_DECOMMIT does not release the address range, and the reserved pages cannot be accessed until they are committed again. MEM_RELEASE requires the original base address and a size of zero. VirtualFree does not fail when the range contains pages in different states, but the entire range originally reserved in one VirtualAlloc call must be released together.
apis.maldev_notes: VirtualFree appears in ordinary cleanup and in analysis of code that releases or decommits regions after use. Its presence is usually less informative than the allocation and protection changes that preceded it.
apis.defensive_notes: Decommit and release events can help explain the lifetime of a memory region. Correlate them with the original allocation and any writes or execution that occurred while the memory was committed.
apis.source_notes: MEM_DECOMMIT and MEM_RELEASE rules checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: VirtualProtect
apis.summary: Changes the protection of a region of committed pages in the calling process.
apis.description: VirtualProtect changes the access protection of committed pages in the calling process. The new protection can make pages read-only, read/write, executable, non-accessible, or guarded, subject to the documented combinations. The previous protection is returned so that the caller can restore it. The function does not change page state, contents, or allocation ownership.
apis.prototype: BOOL VirtualProtect(LPVOID lpAddress, SIZE_T dwSize, DWORD flNewProtect, PDWORD lpflOldProtect);

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The base address of the region whose protection should change. The address is rounded down to a page boundary.

parameters.name: dwSize
parameters.description: The size of the region, in bytes. Every page containing part of the range changes protection, so a range that straddles a page boundary affects both pages. The whole range must lie within a single reserved allocation.

parameters.name: flNewProtect
parameters.description: The new memory protection, such as PAGE_READONLY, PAGE_READWRITE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, or PAGE_NOACCESS. PAGE_GUARD can be combined with an access protection.

parameters.name: lpflOldProtect
parameters.description: Receives the previous protection value of the first page in the region. This parameter must not be NULL, even when the old value is not needed.

return.success: A nonzero value; the protection was changed and lpflOldProtect contains the previous value.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: VirtualProtect operates only on committed pages in the calling process. A range that spans two separately reserved allocations fails, and protection changes do not affect pages that are only reserved. Callers that temporarily change protection should restore the original value when finished.
apis.maldev_notes: Protection changes are common in debuggers, run-time patching, and just-in-time compilers, and they also appear in analysis of code that adjusts memory before writing or executing it. Analysts typically compare the old and new protection with the region's type and later access.
apis.defensive_notes: Protection-change telemetry can show transitions to writable or executable permissions. Recording the requesting module, old and new values, region type, and subsequent execution or writes is more useful than the change alone.
apis.source_notes: Prototype, range restrictions, and the non-NULL lpflOldProtect requirement checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: VirtualQuery
apis.summary: Returns information about a range of pages in the calling process's virtual address space.
apis.description: VirtualQuery describes the memory region that contains a given address. It reports the page state (free, reserved, or committed), the protection, the type of backing (image, mapped file, or private), the allocation base, and the size of the region. The result is written to a MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION structure supplied by the caller.
apis.prototype: SIZE_T VirtualQuery(LPCVOID lpAddress, PMEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION lpBuffer, SIZE_T dwLength);

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The address to query. The function rounds the value down to a page boundary before examining the containing region.

parameters.name: lpBuffer
parameters.description: A pointer to a MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION structure that receives the page information.

parameters.name: dwLength
parameters.description: The size of the buffer, in bytes. Use sizeof(MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION) for the structure declared by the SDK.

return.success: The number of bytes written to the buffer.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: Repeated queries can walk the address space: after each successful call, add the returned RegionSize to the queried address to reach the next region. The Type member distinguishes image-backed, mapped, and private memory, which is often the most useful field for analysis.
apis.maldev_notes: VirtualQuery is used by memory scanners, debuggers, and inspection tools to map regions in the current process. Its presence is routine; the resulting region types and protections are more informative than the call itself.
apis.defensive_notes: Memory maps help explain whether an address belongs to a loaded image, a mapped file, or private memory. This context is valuable when interpreting allocations, protection changes, and execution.

apis.name: VirtualLock
apis.summary: Locks a region of committed pages in the process working set so it is not paged to disk.
apis.description: VirtualLock asks the memory manager to keep the specified committed pages in physical memory until they are unlocked or the process terminates. Locking does not change protection or make inaccessible memory usable, and it is not a security boundary. It is typically used for small buffers that must avoid paging delays.
apis.prototype: BOOL VirtualLock(LPVOID lpAddress, SIZE_T dwSize);

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The base address of the region to lock. The pages must already be committed in the calling process.

parameters.name: dwSize
parameters.description: The size of the region to lock, in bytes. Every page containing part of the range is locked, so a range that straddles a page boundary affects both pages.

return.success: A nonzero value; the pages are locked in the working set.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: All pages in the region must be committed, and memory protected with PAGE_NOACCESS cannot be locked. The maximum number of pages a process can lock is derived from its minimum working set size; applications that need to lock more pages must first increase the working-set limits. Locking pages consumes physical memory and can degrade system performance for other processes.
apis.maldev_notes: VirtualLock occasionally appears in analysis of code that tries to keep buffers out of the paging file. It does not encrypt data, hide memory from other processes, or prevent memory capture; it only affects paging behavior.
apis.defensive_notes: Locking pages is ordinary in performance-sensitive and cryptographic software. Treat it as context rather than as an indicator by itself, and interpret it alongside the buffer's contents and lifetime.
apis.source_notes: Locking semantics and the documented default page limit checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: VirtualUnlock
apis.summary: Unlocks a region of pages previously locked with VirtualLock.
apis.description: VirtualUnlock releases pages from the locked working-set state established by VirtualLock. Once unlocked, the pages become eligible to be paged to disk again. The range must correspond to pages that were previously locked; unlocking other memory fails.
apis.prototype: BOOL VirtualUnlock(LPVOID lpAddress, SIZE_T dwSize);

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The base address of the region to unlock. The range must lie within pages previously locked by VirtualLock.

parameters.name: dwSize
parameters.description: The size of the region to unlock, in bytes. Every page containing part of the range is unlocked.

return.success: A nonzero value; the pages are no longer locked.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: Virtual pages have no lock count, so a single VirtualUnlock covering the locked range is sufficient; multiple unlock calls are not required. Unlocking a range that was not previously locked is reported as a failure.
apis.maldev_notes: VirtualUnlock is ordinary cleanup for code that uses VirtualLock. It is rarely significant on its own and is best read as the end of a buffer's locked lifetime.
apis.defensive_notes: Unlock events can help establish when a process stopped protecting a buffer from paging. They are meaningful mainly in relation to the earlier lock and the buffer's use.
apis.source_notes: Locked-range requirement and return convention checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: VirtualAllocEx
apis.summary: Reserves, commits, or changes the state of a region of memory in another process's virtual address space.
apis.description: VirtualAllocEx performs the same allocation operations as VirtualAlloc, but in the address space of a process identified by a handle. The caller needs PROCESS_VM_OPERATION access to the target. The returned address is valid in the target process and cannot be dereferenced directly by the caller; the region is normally accessed with ReadProcessMemory or WriteProcessMemory.
apis.prototype: LPVOID VirtualAllocEx(HANDLE hProcess, LPVOID lpAddress, SIZE_T dwSize, DWORD flAllocationType, DWORD flProtect);

parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the target process. The handle must have PROCESS_VM_OPERATION access.

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The requested base address in the target process, or NULL to let the system choose one. The address is interpreted in the target's address space.

parameters.name: dwSize
parameters.description: The size of the region, in bytes. When lpAddress is NULL, the system rounds the size up to the next page boundary; otherwise every page containing part of the range is included.

parameters.name: flAllocationType
parameters.description: The allocation operation, such as MEM_RESERVE, MEM_COMMIT, or both, interpreted as for VirtualAlloc.

parameters.name: flProtect
parameters.description: The protection for the committed pages in the target process, such as PAGE_READWRITE or PAGE_EXECUTE_READ.

return.success: The base address of the allocated region in the target process's address space.
return.failure: NULL. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: The returned pointer refers to the target process, not the caller, so it must be passed to APIs that operate on that process rather than dereferenced locally. The region must be released in the target process with VirtualFreeEx, because VirtualFree affects only the calling process. Newly committed pages are zero-initialized.
apis.maldev_notes: VirtualAllocEx is used by debuggers, instrumentation, and tools that manage another process's memory, and it also appears in analysis of cross-process memory operations. The call establishes only that a region was reserved or committed in a target process; the requested protection and later use provide the context.
apis.defensive_notes: Cross-process allocation can be correlated with the caller's identity, the target process, the requested protection, and subsequent reads, writes, or thread creation. None of those elements alone proves intent.
apis.source_notes: Access requirement, address-space semantics, and remote release behavior checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: VirtualProtectEx
apis.summary: Changes the protection of committed pages in another process's virtual address space.
apis.description: VirtualProtectEx changes the access protection of committed pages in a target process. The caller must have PROCESS_VM_OPERATION access to that process. As with VirtualProtect, the previous protection is returned so the caller can restore it, and the range must lie within a single reserved allocation in the target.
apis.prototype: BOOL VirtualProtectEx(HANDLE hProcess, LPVOID lpAddress, SIZE_T dwSize, DWORD flNewProtect, PDWORD lpflOldProtect);

parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the target process. The handle must have PROCESS_VM_OPERATION access.

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The base address of the region in the target process. The address is rounded down to a page boundary.

parameters.name: dwSize
parameters.description: The size of the region, in bytes. Every page containing part of the range changes protection, and the range must stay within one reserved allocation.

parameters.name: flNewProtect
parameters.description: The new protection for the target pages, such as PAGE_READWRITE, PAGE_EXECUTE_READ, or PAGE_NOACCESS.

parameters.name: lpflOldProtect
parameters.description: Receives the previous protection of the first page in the region. This parameter must not be NULL.

return.success: A nonzero value; the protection was changed and lpflOldProtect contains the previous value.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: VirtualProtectEx changes only pages that are committed in the target process. Protection changes do not alter page contents or the allocation's base address. Callers that temporarily relax protection should restore the original value when the operation is complete.
apis.maldev_notes: Protection changes in another process are common in debuggers, hooking frameworks, and patching tools, and they are also examined in analysis of cross-process memory modification. Analysts typically pair the change with the region's previous protection and later access.
apis.defensive_notes: Record the old and new protection, the target process, and the region type. A protection change is most meaningful when correlated with subsequent writes, reads, or execution in the same region.
apis.source_notes: Access requirement and protection semantics checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: ReadProcessMemory
apis.summary: Copies memory from a specified process into the calling process's buffer.
apis.description: ReadProcessMemory reads a block of memory from a target process into a buffer owned by the caller. The handle must have PROCESS_VM_READ access. The entire requested range must be accessible in the target; if any part is not, the operation fails rather than returning a partial copy. The current-process pseudo-handle can be used to read the caller's own memory.
apis.prototype: BOOL ReadProcessMemory(HANDLE hProcess, LPCVOID lpBaseAddress, LPVOID lpBuffer, SIZE_T nSize, SIZE_T *lpNumberOfBytesRead);

parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the process to read from. The handle must have PROCESS_VM_READ access.

parameters.name: lpBaseAddress
parameters.description: The base address in the target process from which to read. The address is interpreted in the target's address space.

parameters.name: lpBuffer
parameters.description: The buffer in the calling process that receives the data. It must be at least nSize bytes.

parameters.name: nSize
parameters.description: The number of bytes to read.

parameters.name: lpNumberOfBytesRead
parameters.description: Optional pointer that receives the number of bytes transferred. It may be NULL when the count is not needed.

return.success: A nonzero value; the requested bytes were copied to lpBuffer.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: The function does not return a partial success: if the range crosses an inaccessible page, the call fails. Reading the calling process's own memory through this API is legal but unnecessary; an ordinary memory copy is simpler and faster.
apis.maldev_notes: ReadProcessMemory appears in debuggers, memory scanners, crash-analysis tools, and analysis of cross-process data collection. Investigators usually focus on the source process, the address range, and the caller's access rather than on the call alone.
apis.defensive_notes: Cross-process read access is visible in handle telemetry and memory-event data. Correlating the reader, the target, the range, and surrounding behavior is more useful than flagging the API by name.

example.title: Read a value from the current process
example.notes: The example reads a local integer through the current-process pseudo-handle, which requires no privileges. The pseudo-handle must not be closed. It is illustrative and is never executed by NtExplorer.

apis.source_notes: All-or-nothing range behavior, access requirement and the optional byte-count parameter checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: WriteProcessMemory
apis.summary: Copies data from the calling process into a specified process's memory.
apis.description: WriteProcessMemory writes a block of data from a caller-owned buffer into a target process. The handle must have PROCESS_VM_WRITE and PROCESS_VM_OPERATION access, and the destination pages must be writable. The entire requested range must be accessible; otherwise the operation fails. The function is used by debuggers, instrumentation, and patching tools.
apis.prototype: BOOL WriteProcessMemory(HANDLE hProcess, LPVOID lpBaseAddress, LPCVOID lpBuffer, SIZE_T nSize, SIZE_T *lpNumberOfBytesWritten);

parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the process to write to. The handle must have PROCESS_VM_WRITE and PROCESS_VM_OPERATION access.

parameters.name: lpBaseAddress
parameters.description: The destination address in the target process. The address is interpreted in the target's address space and must refer to writable memory.

parameters.name: lpBuffer
parameters.description: The buffer in the calling process that contains the data to write. It must be at least nSize bytes.

parameters.name: nSize
parameters.description: The number of bytes to write.

parameters.name: lpNumberOfBytesWritten
parameters.description: Optional pointer that receives the number of bytes transferred. It may be NULL when the count is not needed.

return.success: A nonzero value; the requested bytes were written to the target process.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: Writing to read-only pages fails; callers that need to modify them must change protection first, for example with VirtualProtectEx, and restore it afterwards. The function copies bytes only and does not synchronize with the target's threads or notify the target process.
apis.maldev_notes: WriteProcessMemory is a general-purpose debugger and patching interface. It appears in analysis of code that modifies another process's memory, where the destination region, the origin of the written data, and any subsequent execution are the relevant questions.
apis.defensive_notes: Cross-process write activity can be inferred from handle access rights and memory events. Correlate the writing process, the target, the address and size, and whether protection was changed before the write.
apis.source_notes: Access requirements, range behavior, and the writable-destination constraint checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: VirtualQueryEx
apis.summary: Returns information about a range of pages in another process's virtual address space.
apis.description: VirtualQueryEx describes the memory region containing an address in a target process. It reports the page state, protection, backing type, allocation base, and region size through a MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION structure. The caller must have PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION access to the target. For the calling process, VirtualQuery provides the same information without a handle.
apis.prototype: SIZE_T VirtualQueryEx(HANDLE hProcess, LPCVOID lpAddress, PMEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION lpBuffer, SIZE_T dwLength);

parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the target process. The handle must have PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION access.

parameters.name: lpAddress
parameters.description: The address to query in the target process. The function rounds the value down to a page boundary.

parameters.name: lpBuffer
parameters.description: A pointer to a MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION structure that receives the page information.

parameters.name: dwLength
parameters.description: The size of the buffer, in bytes. Use sizeof(MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION).

return.success: The number of bytes written to the buffer.
return.failure: Zero. Call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: The allocation base and region size in the result refer to the target process's address space. Repeating the call with address plus RegionSize walks the target's regions. For the calling process, VirtualQuery returns the same information without requiring a process handle.
apis.maldev_notes: VirtualQueryEx is used by memory scanners, debuggers, and security tools to enumerate regions in another process. Analysts use its output to distinguish image-backed, mapped, and private memory and to plan or explain later reads and writes.
apis.defensive_notes: Region maps provide context for cross-process reads and writes. They are especially useful when paired with the requesting process, the access rights used, and the operations that follow.
apis.source_notes: Access requirement and MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION reporting checked against Microsoft Learn.

apis.name: CreateFileMappingA
apis.summary: Creates or opens a named or unnamed file mapping object for a specified file.
apis.description: Creates or opens a named or unnamed file mapping object for a specified file. To specify the NUMA node for the physical memory, see CreateFileMappingNuma.
apis.prototype: HANDLE CreateFileMappingA(HANDLE hFile, LPSECURITY_ATTRIBUTES lpFileMappingAttributes, DWORD flProtect, DWORD dwMaximumSizeHigh, DWORD dwMaximumSizeLow, LPCSTR lpName);

parameters.name: hFile
parameters.description: A handle to the file from which to create a file mapping object. The file must be opened with access rights that are compatible with the protection flags that the flProtect parameter specifies. It is not required, but it is recommended that files you intend to map be opened for exclusive access. For more information, see File Security and Access Rights. If hFile is INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE, the calling process must also specify a size for the file mapping object in the dwMaximumSizeHigh and dwMaximumSizeLow parameters. In this scenario, CreateFileMapping creates a file mapping object of a specified size that is backed by the system paging file instead of by a file in the file system.

parameters.name: lpFileMappingAttributes
parameters.description: A pointer to a SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES structure that determines whether a returned handle can be inherited by child processes. The lpSecurityDescriptor member of the SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES structure specifies a security descriptor for a new file mapping object. If lpFileMappingAttributes is NULL, the handle cannot be inherited and the file mapping object gets a default security descriptor. The access control lists (ACL) in the default security descriptor for a file mapping object come from the primary or impersonation token of the creator. For more information, see File Mapping Security and Access Rights.

parameters.name: flProtect
parameters.description: Specifies the page protection of the file mapping object. All mapped views of the object must be compatible with this protection. This parameter can be one of the following values. Value Meaning PAGE_EXECUTE_READ 0x20 Allows views to be mapped for read-only, copy-on-write, or execute access. The file handle specified by the hFile parameter must be created with the GENERIC_READ and GENERIC_EXECUTE access rights. Windows Server 2003 and Windows XP: This value is not available until Windows XP with SP2 and Windows Server 2003 with SP1. PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE 0x40 Allows views to be mapped for read-only, copy-on-write, read/write, or execute access. The file handle that the hFile parameter specifies must be created with the GENERIC_READ, GENERIC_WRITE, and GENERIC_EXECUTE access rights. Windows Server 2003 and Windows XP: This value is not available until Windows XP with SP2 and Windows Serv

parameters.name: dwMaximumSizeHigh
parameters.description: The high-order DWORD of the maximum size of the file mapping object.

parameters.name: dwMaximumSizeLow
parameters.description: The low-order DWORD of the maximum size of the file mapping object. If this parameter and dwMaximumSizeHigh are 0 (zero), the maximum size of the file mapping object is equal to the current size of the file that hFile identifies. An attempt to map a file with a length of 0 (zero) fails with an error code of ERROR_FILE_INVALID. Applications should test for files with a length of 0 (zero) and reject those files.

parameters.name: lpName
parameters.description: The name of the file mapping object. If this parameter matches the name of an existing mapping object, the function requests access to the object with the protection that flProtect specifies. If this parameter is NULL, the file mapping object is created without a name. If lpName matches the name of an existing event, semaphore, mutex, waitable timer, or job object, the function fails, and the GetLastError function returns ERROR_INVALID_HANDLE. This occurs because these objects share the same namespace. The name can have a "Global\" or "Local\" prefix to explicitly create the object in the global or session namespace. The remainder of the name can contain any character except the backslash character (\). Creating a file mapping object in the global namespace from a session other than session zero requires the SeCreateGlobalPrivilege privilege. For more information, see Kernel Object Name

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is a handle to the newly created file mapping object.
return.failure: If the object exists before the function call, the function returns a handle to the existing object (with its current size, not the specified size), and GetLastError returns ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS. If the function fails, the return value is NULL. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: After a file mapping object is created, the size of the file must not exceed the size of the file mapping object; if it does, not all of the file contents are available for sharing. If an application specifies a size for the file mapping object that is larger than the size of the actual named file on disk and if the page protection allows write access (that is, the flProtect parameter specifies PAGE_READWRITE or PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE), then the file on disk is increased to match the specified size of the file mapping object. If the file is extended, the contents of the file between the old end of the file and the new end of the file are not guaranteed to be zero; the behavior is defined by the file system. If the file on disk cannot be increased, CreateFileMapping fails and GetLastError returns ERROR_DISK_FULL. The initial contents of the pages in a file mapping object backed by the operating system paging file are 0 (zero). The handle that CreateFileMapping returns has full access to a new file mapping object, and can be used with any function that requires a handle to a file mapping object. Multiple processes can share a view of the same file by either using a single shared file mapping object or creating separate file mapping objects backed by the same file. apis.name: GetProcessHeap
apis.summary: Retrieves a handle to the default heap of the calling process.
apis.description: Retrieves a handle to the default heap of the calling process. This handle can then be used in subsequent calls to the heap functions.
apis.prototype: HANDLE GetProcessHeap(VOID);

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is a handle to the calling process's heap.
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is NULL. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: The GetProcessHeap function obtains a handle to the default heap for the calling process. A process can use this handle to allocate memory from the process heap without having to first create a private heap using the HeapCreate function. Modified pages in the unmapped view are not written to disk until their share count reaches zero, or in other words, until they are unmapped or trimmed from the working sets of all processes that share the pages. Although an application may close the file handle used to create a file mapping object, the system holds the corresponding file open until the last view of the file is unmapped. apis.name: VirtualProtectFromApp
apis.summary: Changes the protection on a region of committed pages in the virtual address space of the calling process.
apis.description: Changes the protection on a region of committed pages in the virtual address space of the calling process.
apis.prototype: BOOL VirtualProtectFromApp(PVOID Address, SIZE_T Size, ULONG NewProtection, PULONG OldProtection);

parameters.name: Address
parameters.description: A pointer an address that describes the starting page of the region of pages whose access protection attributes are to be changed. All pages in the specified region must be within the same reserved region allocated when calling the VirtualAlloc, VirtualAllocFromApp, or VirtualAllocEx function using MEM_RESERVE. The pages cannot span adjacent reserved regions that were allocated by separate calls to VirtualAlloc, VirtualAllocFromApp, or VirtualAllocEx using MEM_RESERVE.

parameters.name: Size
parameters.description: The size of the region whose access protection attributes are to be changed, in bytes. The region of affected pages includes all pages containing one or more bytes in the range from the Address parameter to (Address+Size). This means that a 2-byte range straddling a page boundary causes the protection attributes of both pages to be changed.

parameters.name: NewProtection
parameters.description: The memory protection option. This parameter can be one of the memory protection constants. For mapped views, this value must be compatible with the access protection specified when the view was mapped (see MapViewOfFile, MapViewOfFileEx, and MapViewOfFileExNuma). The following constants generate an error: PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE PAGE_EXECUTE_WRITECOPY The following constants are allowed only for apps that have the codeGeneration capability: PAGE_EXECUTE PAGE_EXECUTE_READ

parameters.name: OldProtection
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the previous access protection value of the first page in the specified region of pages. If this parameter is NULL or does not point to a valid variable, the function fails.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is nonzero.
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is zero. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: You can call VirtualProtectFromApp from Windows Store apps with just-in-time (JIT) capabilities to use JIT functionality. The app must include the codeGeneration capability in the app manifest file to use JIT capabilities. You can set the access protection value on committed pages only. If the state of any page in the specified region is not committed, the function fails and returns without modifying the access protection of any pages in the specified region. The PAGE_GUARD protection modifier establishes guard pages. Guard pages act as one-shot access alarms. For more information, see Creating Guard Pages. It is best to avoid using VirtualProtectFromApp to change page protections on memory blocks allocated by GlobalAlloc, HeapAlloc, or LocalAlloc, because multiple memory blocks can exist on a single page. The heap manager assumes that all pages in the heap grant at least read and write access. VirtualProtectFromApp allows you to mark pages as executable, but does not allow you to set both write and execute permissions at the same time. When protecting a region that will be executable, the calling program bears responsibility for ensuring cache coherency via an appropriate call to FlushInstructionCache once the code has been set in place. Otherwise attempts to execute code out of the newly executable region may produce unpredictable results.

apis.name: CreateRemoteThread
apis.summary: Creates a thread that runs in the virtual address space of another process.
apis.description: Creates a thread that runs in the virtual address space of another process. Use the CreateRemoteThreadEx function to create a thread that runs in the virtual address space of another process and optionally specify extended attributes.
apis.prototype: HANDLE CreateRemoteThread(HANDLE hProcess, LPSECURITY_ATTRIBUTES lpThreadAttributes, SIZE_T dwStackSize, LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE lpStartAddress, LPVOID lpParameter, DWORD dwCreationFlags, LPDWORD lpThreadId);

parameters.name: hProcess
parameters.description: A handle to the process in which the thread is to be created. The handle must have the PROCESS_CREATE_THREAD, PROCESS_QUERY_INFORMATION, PROCESS_VM_OPERATION, PROCESS_VM_WRITE, and PROCESS_VM_READ access rights, and may fail without these rights on certain platforms. For more information, see Process Security and Access Rights.

parameters.name: lpThreadAttributes
parameters.description: A pointer to a SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES structure that specifies a security descriptor for the new thread and determines whether child processes can inherit the returned handle. If *lpThreadAttributes* is NULL, the thread gets a default security descriptor and the handle cannot be inherited. The access control lists (ACL) in the default security descriptor for a thread come from the primary token of the creator.

parameters.name: dwStackSize
parameters.description: The initial size of the stack, in bytes. The system rounds this value to the nearest page. If this parameter is 0 (zero), the new thread uses the default size for the executable. For more information, see Thread Stack Size.

parameters.name: lpStartAddress
parameters.description: A pointer to the application-defined function of type LPTHREAD_START_ROUTINE to be executed by the thread and represents the starting address of the thread in the remote process. The function must exist in the remote process. For more information, see ThreadProc.

parameters.name: lpParameter
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable to be passed to the thread function.

parameters.name: dwCreationFlags
parameters.description: The flags that control the creation of the thread. Value Meaning 0 The thread runs immediately after creation. CREATE_SUSPENDED 0x00000004 The thread is created in a suspended state, and does not run until the ResumeThread function is called. STACK_SIZE_PARAM_IS_A_RESERVATION 0x00010000 The dwStackSize parameter specifies the initial reserve size of the stack. If this flag is not specified, dwStackSize specifies the commit size.

parameters.name: lpThreadId
parameters.description: A pointer to a variable that receives the thread identifier. If this parameter is NULL, the thread identifier is not returned.

return.success: If the function succeeds, the return value is a handle to the new thread. Note that CreateRemoteThread may succeed even if lpStartAddress points to data, code, or is not accessible. If the start address is invalid when the thread runs, an exception occurs, and the thread terminates. Thread termination due to a invalid start address is handled as an error exit for the thread's process. This behavior is similar to the asynchronous nature of CreateProcess, where the process is created even if it refers to invalid or missing dynamic-link libraries (DLL).
return.failure: If the function fails, the return value is NULL. To get extended error information, call GetLastError.

apis.remarks: The CreateRemoteThread function causes a new thread of execution to begin in the address space of the specified process. The thread has access to all objects that the process opens. Prior to Windows 8, Terminal Services isolates each terminal session by design. Therefore, CreateRemoteThread fails if the target process is in a different session than the calling process. The new thread handle is created with full access to the new thread. If a security descriptor is not provided, the handle may be used in any function that requires a thread object handle. When a security descriptor is provided, an access check is performed on all subsequent uses of the handle before access is granted. If the access check denies access, the requesting process cannot use the handle to gain access to the thread. If the thread is created in a runnable state (that is, if the CREATE_SUSPENDED flag is not used), the thread can start running before CreateThread returns and, in particular, before the caller receives the handle and identifier of the created thread. The thread is created with a thread priority of THREAD_PRIORITY_NORMAL. Use the GetThreadPriority and SetThreadPriority functions to get and set the priority value of a thread. When a thread terminates, the thread object attains a signaled state, which satisfies the threads that are waiting for the object. The thread object remains in the system
